claim: The purity of all AMG lipids was >=90% as judged by LC-MS.
locus_a: SI p.5, 'General procedure for synthesis of the ionizable lipids'
locus_b: The SI's own printed 'LC-MS purity' values: 146 of them, minimum 85%, median 96%. Three fall below 90% - AMG124 89% (p.107), AMG134 85% (p.107), AMG1741 89% (p.119).
what_we_emitted: Nothing. None of those three lipids carries a value we emit: AMG124 and AMG134 appear in no value panel, and AMG1741's structure is not established (see DECISIONS D-2).
why: The blanket statement is contradicted by three of the SI's own numbers. It changes no emitted value, but it is the kind of global assurance that gets quoted in Methods, so it is recorded rather than silently passed on. Check P8 in 07_qc.json fails on exactly this.

claim: lipid AMG104 yielded the highest mRNA expression and outperformed the next best lipid AMG1010 by ~5-fold
locus_a: Article, Results, 'In Vitro and In Vivo Screening of AMG Lipid Library' (PMC13387048)
locus_b: Source Data MOESM3 'Figure 1' rows 27-29: the screen-3 panel contains Head 8/9/10 x Tail 4/Tail 5 only - that is AMG84, AMG85, AMG94, AMG95, AMG104, AMG105. AMG1010 is not in it. Means: AMG104 5.469e8, AMG105 1.161e8 (ratio 4.71), AMG94 4.054e6, AMG95 5.231e7, AMG84 6.69e6, AMG85 1.517e7.
what_we_emitted: The six panel values, each keyed to the lipid its own row and column label name. Nothing that depends on the sentence.
why: Two readings are possible and the sources do not choose between them: either the text's 'AMG1010' is a slip for AMG105, or the Source Data's 'Tail 5' column header is wrong. The ~5-fold is reproduced exactly by AMG104/AMG105 = 4.71, which favours the first, but the same preceding paragraph says screen 2 selected tails G4, G5 and G10, so a G10 member in screen 3 is not absurd. Queued as DECISIONS D-4.

locus_a: NIH author manuscript (PMC13387048) Figure 1 legend: 'c,d,e ... batch-based screen 1 (c), screen 2 (d), and screen 3 of individual top-performing lipids (e)'
locus_b: Publisher Source Data MOESM3 'Figure 1' labels the same three blocks 1d, 1e and 1f.
what_we_emitted: The Source Data lettering (1d/1e/1f), because that is the file the values come from; every row records its workbook, sheet and cell range.
why: The author manuscript is the accepted version and the published figure gained a panel before it. A reader following the author-manuscript letters to our 'Figure 1f' would land on screen 2. Recorded so the mapping is explicit rather than inferred.

claim: HRMS of AMG106: m/z 1843.7177 (calculated for C114H226N4O12 [M+H]+ 1843.7197)
locus_b: The quoted ion C114H226N4O12 implies a neutral C114H225N4O12, whose degree of unsaturation is 4.5 - not an integer, so no such molecule exists. Our reconstruction, which re-assembles exactly from an Am10 block read 27 times and a G6 block read 10 times, is C114H224N4O12, [M+H]+ 1842.7114.
what_we_emitted: Our structure, flagged in 02_structures.csv as the one HRMS FAIL inside the 10x10 grid (546 ppm).
why: The printed m/z and the printed formula agree with each other to 1.1 ppm, so the error is in the composition the authors computed, not in a typo of the mass. Every other G6 lipid (AMG16, AMG26, ... AMG96) passes its own HRMS, which is what makes the G6 block trustworthy here.

claim: HRMS of AMG1441: m/z 736.6107 (calculated for C42H80N4O6 [M+H]+ 736.6077)
locus_b: 736.6078 is the NEUTRAL exact mass of C42H80N4O6; its [M+H]+ is 737.6156. The printed value is therefore the neutral mass carrying an [M+H]+ label.
what_we_emitted: Nothing - AMG1441's structure is not established (DECISIONS D-2), so no row is emitted for it.
why: The ion label and the number disagree by exactly one proton. It is recorded because the same ambiguity ([M+H]+ vs neutral) is what makes a formula-string comparison unreliable across this SI, and is why stage01 gates on the m/z rather than on the formula.

claim: HRMS of AMG1541-OHD: m/z 1689.652 (calculated for C102H187N6O12 [M+H]+ ...)
locus_b: The [M+H]+ of C102H187N6O12 is 1688.4207. The printed 1689.652 is 1.23 Da (729 ppm) away from the formula printed beside it. The SAME formula appears for AMG1559 (SI p.115) with m/z 1688.4221, which matches it to 0.8 ppm.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. Neither AMG1541-OHD nor AMG1559 carries a value we emit.
why: One of the two entries carries a mistyped mass. AMG1541-OHD and AMG1559 are genuinely isomers - the OH-deleted lipid and the Michael-addition lipid have the same composition - so the duplicate formula is correct and only the mass is not.

claim: 'we then synthesized and purified (>90% purity) all 100 of the ionizable lipids from this initial library'
locus_b: The SI's characterization section (pp.44-121) draws and characterises 96 of the 100. AMG41, AMG43, AMG73 and AMG83 appear nowhere in it - no structure, no NMR, no HRMS - although all four carry a value in Extended Figure 1.
what_we_emitted: Those four as enumerated structures built from their Am and G blocks, each block independently derived from other members of the same row and column, carrying confidence = medium and structure_assumed = 1 with a note saying the SI draws nothing for them.
why: The claim and the SI disagree about whether all 100 were made and characterised. The values exist for all 100, so the four are emitted rather than dropped, but a reader must be able to see that their structures rest on the library rule and not on a drawing.

claim: 'A combinatorial library of 100 unique ionizable lipids'
locus_b: Supplementary Table 2's naming rule (AMG11 = Am1+G1, AMG510 = Am5+G10, AMG104 = Am10+G4, AMG1541 = Am15+G41) is not injective over the library's own alphabet: AMG141 parses as Am1+G41 AND as Am14+G1, and both blocks exist.
what_we_emitted: Am1+G41, decided from the DRAWN structure: its headgroup matches the Am1 block (eleven independent reads) and its arm matches the G41 block (seven), while Am14+G1 matches neither.
why: A name that two real block pairs can produce is a collision waiting for whoever keys on the label. Resolved by structure, never by preference - putting a measured value on the wrong molecule because a name looked obvious is the AC_2025 failure. Recorded in 02_blocks_consensus.json under 'resolved_by_structure'.

claim: Extended Figure 1 reports an RFU for every one of the 100 lipids
locus_b: Two cells are exactly 0.0000 with Stdev 0.0000 and n = 3: AMG41 (G1 x Am4) and AMG51 (G1 x Am5).
what_we_emitted: Both rows, with value_is_bound = upper and a note saying the published value is the assay floor and not a measurement of zero.
why: A zero luminescence reading is a censored observation, not a quantity. It also cannot be log-transformed, which the corpus's z-of-log10 convention requires - see DECISIONS D-5.
